"""Download + extract the authors' CRAN package `otsfeatures` (source of the data
and of the reference R implementations of the feature functions).

Reusable raw artefacts are cached in $REPRO_DATA_CACHE so repeat runs are offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import urllib.request

PKG = "otsfeatures"
PACKAGES_URL = "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES"
CONTRIB_URL = "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/"

# Files the reproduction needs out of the package tarball.
REQUIRED = [
    "data/SyntheticData2.RData",
    "R/c_marginal_probabilities.R",
    "R/c_joint_probabilities.R",
    "R/marginal_probabilities.R",
    "R/joint_probabilities.R",
    "R/auxiliary_f_i_j_k.R",
    "R/auxiliary_p_i_j_k.R",
    "R/check_ots.R",
]


def cache_dir() -> str:
    d = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data", "_cache")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _md5(path: str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def cran_latest() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return (version, md5) of the current CRAN source tarball, best effort."""
    txt = urllib.request.urlopen(PACKAGES_URL, timeout=60).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    m = re.search(rf"^Package:\s*{PKG}\s*$(.*?)(?=^Package:|\Z)", txt, re.M | re.S)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{PKG} not found on CRAN PACKAGES index")
    block = m.group(1)
    ver = re.search(r"^Version:\s*(\S+)", block, re.M)
    md5 = re.search(r"^MD5sum:\s*(\S+)", block, re.M)
    if not ver:
        raise RuntimeError("could not parse Version from CRAN PACKAGES")
    return ver.group(1), (md5.group(1) if md5 else "")


def download_tarball(dest_dir: str) -> str:
    """Fetch the CRAN source tarball (or reuse the shared cache); return its path."""
    cdir = cache_dir()
    version, md5 = cran_latest()
    fname = f"{PKG}_{version}.tar.gz"
    cached = os.path.join(cdir, fname)
    if os.path.exists(cached) and (not md5 or _md5(cached) == md5):
        print(f"[download] reusing cached tarball {cached}")
        local = os.path.join(dest_dir, fname)
        if os.path.abspath(local) != os.path.abspath(cached):
            shutil.copyfile(cached, local)
        return local
    url = CONTRIB_URL + fname
    print(f"[download] {url}")
    tmp = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), fname)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r, open(tmp, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(r.read())
    if md5 and _md5(tmp) != md5:
        raise RuntimeError(f"MD5 mismatch for {fname}")
    for p in (cached, os.path.join(dest_dir, fname)):
        if os.path.abspath(p) != os.path.abspath(tmp):
            shutil.copyfile(tmp, p)
    return os.path.join(dest_dir, fname)


def extract(tar_path: str, out_root: str) -> str:
    """Extract the tarball; return the package source directory."""
    pkg_dir = os.path.join(out_root, PKG)
    if os.path.isdir(pkg_dir) and all(
        os.path.exists(os.path.join(pkg_dir, r)) for r in REQUIRED
    ):
        print(f"[extract] reusing already extracted {pkg_dir}")
        return pkg_dir
    if os.path.isdir(out_root):
        shutil.rmtree(out_root)
    os.makedirs(out_root, exist_ok=True)
    with tarfile.open(tar_path, "r:gz") as tf:
        try:
            tf.extractall(out_root, filter="data")  # no symlinks / path escapes
        except TypeError:  # Python < 3.12
            tf.extractall(out_root)
    missing = [r for r in REQUIRED if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(pkg_dir, r))]
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"extracted tarball is missing: {missing}")
    print(f"[extract] OK -> {pkg_dir}")
    return pkg_dir


def get_package_source(out_root: str) -> str:
    """Download (cached) + extract, return path to the extracted `otsfeatures` dir."""
    os.makedirs(out_root, exist_ok=True)
    tar_path = download_tarball(out_root)
    return extract(tar_path, out_root)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data")
    print(get_package_source(root))

"""Download + extract the authors' CRAN package `otsfeatures`.

It is the source of both the bundled `SyntheticData2` collection and the reference
R implementations of `c_marginal_probabilities` / `c_joint_probabilities` that this
reproduction ports to Python.

Idempotent and offline-friendly: if $REPRO_DATA_CACHE already holds the tarball it is
reused (no network); otherwise the CRAN source tarball is fetched and cached.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import urllib.request

PKG = "otsfeatures"
PACKAGES_URL = "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES"
CONTRIB_URL = "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/"
FALLBACK_VERSION = "1.0.0"  # version used in the paper; used only for cache probing

REQUIRED = [
    "DESCRIPTION",
    "data/SyntheticData2.RData",
    "R/c_marginal_probabilities.R",
    "R/c_joint_probabilities.R",
    "R/marginal_probabilities.R",
    "R/joint_probabilities.R",
    "R/auxiliary_f_i_j_k.R",
    "R/auxiliary_p_i_j_k.R",
    "R/check_ots.R",
]


def cache_dir() -> str:
    d = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data", "_cache")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _md5(path: str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def _find_cached_tarball() -> str | None:
    """Any already-cached otsfeatures_*.tar.gz, newest version first."""
    cdir = cache_dir()
    hits = [
        os.path.join(cdir, f)
        for f in os.listdir(cdir)
        if f.startswith(f"{PKG}_") and f.endswith(".tar.gz")
    ]
    if not hits:
        return None
    def ver_key(p):
        m = re.match(rf"{PKG}_(.+)\.tar\.gz$", os.path.basename(p))
        return tuple(int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in re.split(r"[.\-]", m.group(1))) if m else (0,)
    return sorted(hits, key=ver_key)[-1]


def cran_latest() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(version, md5) of the current CRAN source tarball; falls back to cached file."""
    try:
        txt = urllib.request.urlopen(PACKAGES_URL, timeout=45).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        m = re.search(rf"^Package:\s*{PKG}\s*$(.*?)(?=^Package:|\Z)", txt, re.M | re.S)
        if m:
            ver = re.search(r"^Version:\s*(\S+)", m.group(1), re.M)
            md5 = re.search(r"^MD5sum:\s*(\S+)", m.group(1), re.M)
            if ver:
                return ver.group(1), (md5.group(1) if md5 else "")
    except Exception as exc:  # offline / index change: use whatever is cached
        print(f"[download] CRAN index unavailable ({exc}); using cached tarball")
    cached = _find_cached_tarball()
    if cached:
        v = re.match(rf"{PKG}_(.+)\.tar\.gz$", os.path.basename(cached)).group(1)
        return v, ""
    return FALLBACK_VERSION, ""


def get_tarball(dest_dir: str) -> str:
    """Ensure the source tarball exists inside `dest_dir`; reuse the shared cache."""
    os.makedirs(dest_dir, exist_ok=True)
    version, md5 = cran_latest()
    fname = f"{PKG}_{version}.tar.gz"
    local = os.path.join(dest_dir, fname)
    if os.path.exists(local) and (not md5 or _md5(local) == md5):
        print(f"[download] already present: {local}")
        return local

    cached = _find_cached_tarball()
    if cached and (not md5 or _md5(cached) == md5):
        print(f"[download] reusing cached tarball {cached}")
        shutil.copyfile(cached, local)
        return local

    url = CONTRIB_URL + fname
    print(f"[download] fetching {url}")
    tmp = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), fname)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=180) as r:
        blob = r.read()
    with open(tmp, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(blob)
    if md5 and _md5(tmp) != md5:
        raise RuntimeError(f"MD5 mismatch for {fname}")
    shutil.copyfile(tmp, local)
    shutil.copyfile(tmp, os.path.join(cache_dir(), fname))  # cache for later runs
    print(f"[download] saved {local} ({len(blob)} bytes)")
    return local


def extract(tar_path: str, out_root: str) -> str:
    """Extract to `<out_root>/otsfeatures` and verify the files we need are present."""
    pkg_dir = os.path.join(out_root, PKG)
    if os.path.isdir(pkg_dir) and all(os.path.exists(os.path.join(pkg_dir, r)) for r in REQUIRED):
        print(f"[extract] reusing extracted sources {pkg_dir}")
        return pkg_dir
    if os.path.isdir(pkg_dir):
        shutil.rmtree(pkg_dir)
    os.makedirs(out_root, exist_ok=True)
    with tarfile.open(tar_path, "r:gz") as tf:
        try:
            tf.extractall(out_root, filter="data")
        except TypeError:  # Python < 3.12
            tf.extractall(out_root)
    missing = [r for r in REQUIRED if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(pkg_dir, r))]
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"extracted tarball is missing: {missing}")
    print(f"[extract] OK -> {pkg_dir}")
    return pkg_dir


def get_package_source(out_root: str) -> str:
    return extract(get_tarball(out_root), out_root)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data")
    print(get_package_source(root))

"""Python port of the parts of the CRAN package `otsfeatures` that the paper's
clustering workflow uses.

Every function here is a line-by-line transcription of the authors' R source shipped
in the tarball (extracted by `download_otsfeatures.py`); the file/line of the original
is quoted in each docstring so the port can be audited.

Transcribed sources
-------------------
otsfeatures/R/c_marginal_probabilities.R  -> c_marginal_probabilities()
otsfeatures/R/c_joint_probabilities.R     -> c_joint_probabilities()
otsfeatures/R/marginal_probabilities.R    -> marginal_probabilities()
otsfeatures/R/joint_probabilities.R       -> joint_probabilities()
otsfeatures/R/auxiliary_f_i_j_k.R         -> f_i_j_k()
otsfeatures/R/auxiliary_p_i_j_k.R         -> p_i_j_k()
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

import numpy as np
import rdata


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- data

def load_ots_collection(rda_path: str, object_name: str | None = None):
    """Load an `otsfeatures` data object ({data: list, classes: vector}) from .RData.

    Returns (list_of_1d_int_arrays, classes_1d_int_array).
    """
    obj = rdata.read_rda(rda_path)
    if object_name is not None:
        obj = obj[object_name]
    else:  # the tarball ships exactly one object per file
        if len(obj) != 1:
            raise RuntimeError(f"expected a single R object in {rda_path}, got {list(obj)}")
        obj = next(iter(obj.values()))
    if "data" not in obj or "classes" not in obj:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{rda_path} does not hold a list with elements data/classes")

    series = [np.asarray(s, dtype=np.float64).ravel() for s in obj["data"]]
    classes = np.asarray(obj["classes"]).ravel().astype(int)
    return series, classes


# --------------------------------------------------------------- auxiliary counts
# otsfeatures/R/auxiliary_f_i_j_k.R
#   a <- series[(k+1):T]; b <- series[1:(T-k)]
#   count[i] <- (a[i] <= i_stat) & (b[i] <= j_stat);  return sum(count)/(T-k)
def f_i_j_k(series: np.ndarray, i_stat: float, j_stat: float, k: int = 1) -> float:
    T = series.shape[0]
    a = series[k:]           # X_t          (t = k+1..T, R indexing)
    b = series[:T - k]       # X_{t-k}
    return float(np.count_nonzero((a <= i_stat) & (b <= j_stat))) / (T - k)


# otsfeatures/R/auxiliary_p_i_j_k.R  (same but with `==` instead of `<=`)
def p_i_j_k(series: np.ndarray, i_stat: float, j_stat: float, k: int = 1) -> float:
    T = series.shape[0]
    a = series[k:]
    b = series[:T - k]
    return float(np.count_nonzero((a == i_stat) & (b == j_stat))) / (T - k)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- features
# otsfeatures/R/c_marginal_probabilities.R:
#   for (i in 1:n_states) marginal[i] <- sum(series <= states[i]) / length(series)
#   return(marginal[-n_states])              # drops the always-1 last entry
def c_marginal_probabilities(series: np.ndarray, states) -> np.ndarray:
    states = np.asarray(states, dtype=np.float64)
    T = series.shape[0]
    out = np.array([np.count_nonzero(series <= s) / T for s in states], dtype=np.float64)
    return out[:-1]                          # f_0, ..., f_{n-1}  -> length n_states-1


# otsfeatures/R/c_joint_probabilities.R:
#   matrix[i,j] <- f_i_j_k_function(series, states[i], states[j], k = lag)  (n x n)
#   return(matrix[-n_states, -n_states])     # drops last row and last column
def c_joint_probabilities(series: np.ndarray, states, lag: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    states = np.asarray(states, dtype=np.float64)
    m = np.array([[f_i_j_k(series, si, sj, lag) for sj in states] for si in states])
    return m[:-1, :-1]


# otsfeatures/R/marginal_probabilities.R: count(series == states[i]) / T, all states kept
def marginal_probabilities(series: np.ndarray, states) -> np.ndarray:
    states = np.asarray(states, dtype=np.float64)
    T = series.shape[0]
    return np.array([np.count_nonzero(series == s) / T for s in states], dtype=np.float64)


# otsfeatures/R/joint_probabilities.R: full (n+1)x(n+1) matrix, nothing dropped
def joint_probabilities(series: np.ndarray, states, lag: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    states = np.asarray(states, dtype=np.float64)
    return np.array([[p_i_j_k(series, si, sj, lag) for sj in states] for si in states])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ datasets
def _row_from_matrix(mat: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """R `unlist()` of a matrix flattens column-major; `matrix(..., byrow=TRUE)` then
    lays that vector out as one row of the dataset (paper Sec. 4.3.2 code, p. 20)."""
    return mat.flatten(order="F")


def build_feature_dataset(series_list, states, lags=(1, 2), cumulative=True):
    """Reproduce `dataset_1` (cumulative, `c_*` functions) or `dataset_2` (PMF).

    Paper, Section 4.3.2:
        dataset_1 <- cbind(dataset_marginal_1, dataset_serial_1_1, dataset_serial_1_2)
    where each block is `matrix(unlist(lapply(...)), nrow = 80, byrow = TRUE)`.
    """
    marg_fn = c_marginal_probabilities if cumulative else marginal_probabilities
    joint_fn = c_joint_probabilities if cumulative else joint_probabilities

    rows = []

        rows.append(np.concatenate(blocks))
    return np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.float64)


def dataset_1(series_list, states=(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), lags=(1, 2)) -> np.ndarray:
    """Cumulative-probability features -> the dCC representation (paper dataset_1)."""
    return build_feature_dataset(series_list, states, lags, cumulative=True)

    """PMF features -> the dPMF representation (paper dataset_2)."""
    return build_feature_dataset(series_list, states, lags, cumulative=False)

"""Deterministic PAM (Partitioning Around Medoids), build + swap.

Port of the algorithm used by the paper: `cluster::pam(distance_matrix, k = 4)`
(R package cluster, Algorithm 3 of Kaufman & Rousseeuw, 1990).

Conventions chosen to match that implementation:
  * BUILD greedily adds the medoid with the largest total gain; ties -> lowest index.
  * SWAP evaluates every (non-medoid, medoid) pair with the classic second-nearest
    medoid cost formula and applies the single best improving swap (steepest
    descent); repeats until no swap reduces the total cost. Ties -> lowest indices.
  * Each object is attached to its nearest medoid; ties -> lowest medoid index.
The procedure is fully deterministic, so no random seed is involved (the paper does
not set one before `pam()` either).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def _build(D: np.ndarray, k: int, must_be_medoid=None):
    n = D.shape[0]
    # first medoid: minimises the sum of distances to all objects
    medoids = [int(np.argmin(D.sum(axis=1)))]
    while len(medoids) < k:
        cur = np.asarray(medoids)
        d1 = D[:, cur].min(axis=1)
        best_gain, best = -np.inf, None
        for i in range(n):
            if i in medoids:
                continue
            dec = np.maximum(0.0, d1 - D[:, i])          # gain if i became a medoid
            gain = dec.sum()
            if gain > best_gain + 1e-12:
                best_gain, best = gain, i
        if best is None:                                  # all gains tie at 0
            best = next(i for i in range(n) if i not in medoids)
        medoids.append(best)
    return medoids


def _labels(D: np.ndarray, medoids):
    md = D[:, medoids]
    lab = md.argmin(axis=1)                # ties -> first (lowest-index) medoid
    cost = md.min(axis=1).sum()
    return lab, cost


def _swap_costs(D: np.ndarray, medoids):
    """Total cost change T(o,m) for swapping non-medoid o in and medoid m out.

    q(j,o,m) = d(j,o) - d(j,m)                                   if d(j,m) <= d(j,o)
             = min(d(j, C2(j)) - d(j,m), d(j,o) - d(j,m))        otherwise
    with C2(j) the second closest medoid to j (m excluded).
    """
    k = len(medoids)
    md = D[:, medoids]
    order = np.argsort(md, axis=1, kind="stable")
    sorted_md = np.take_along_axis(md, order, axis=1)
    nearest_med_idx = order[:, 0]
    second_med_idx = np.where(order[:, 1] == order[:, 0], order[:, 2], order[:, 1])
    # distance from j to its closest medoid other than the one it is attached to
    d2 = sorted_md[:, 1]

    costs = np.empty((n := D.shape[0], k), dtype=np.float64)
    for m_pos, m in enumerate(medoids):
        dm = md[:, m_pos]
        # closest medoid other than m for every object
        other_pos = np.array([p for p in range(k) if p != m_pos])
        d_other = md[:, other_pos].min(axis=1)
        for o in range(n):
            if o in medoids:
                continue
            do = D[:, o]
            q = np.where(do <= dm, do - dm, np.minimum(d_other - dm, do - dm))
            q[m] = 0.0                      # the swapped-out medoid joins o itself
            costs[o, m_pos] = q.sum()
    del nearest_med_idx, second_med_idx
    return costs


def pam(D, k: int, max_iter: int = 1000):
    """Run PAM on a square dissimilarity matrix.

    Returns dict with 'medoids' (indices), 'labels' (0-based, by medoid order) and
    'cost' (sum of distances of objects to their assigned medoid).
    """
    D = np.asarray(D, dtype=np.float64)
    n = D.shape[0]
    if D.shape[0] != D.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError("D must be a square dissimilarity matrix")
    if not (1 <= k <= n):
        raise ValueError("k must be between 1 and n")

    medoids = _build(D, k)
    labels, cost = _labels(D, medoids)

    for _ in range(max_iter):
        costs = _swap_costs(D, medoids)
        # consider only swaps of a non-medoid object with a medoid
        mask = np.ones_like(costs, dtype=bool)
        for pos, m in enumerate(medoids):
            mask[m, pos] = False
        costs_masked = np.where(mask, costs, np.inf)
        flat = costs_masked.argmin()
        o, m_pos = divmod(int(flat), len(medoids))
        if costs_masked[o, m_pos] >= -1e-12:
            break
        new_medoids = list(medoids)
        new_medoids[m_pos] = o
        new_medoids = sorted(new_medoids)
        new_labels, new_cost = _labels(D, new_medoids)
        if new_cost >= cost - 1e-12:        # safeguard against cycling
            break
        medoids, labels, cost = new_medoids, new_labels, new_cost

    return {"medoids": [int(m) for m in medoids],
            "labels": np.asarray(labels, dtype=int),
            "cost": float(cost)}


def pam_from_condensed(dcond, k: int, n: int):
    from scipy.spatial.distance import squareform
    return pam(squareform(dcond), k)

def _swap_costs(D: np.ndarray, medoids):
    """Total cost change T(o,m) for swapping non-medoid o in and medoid m out.

    Kaufman & Rousseeuw's exchange procedure: only objects currently attached to m
    change their attachment when m leaves, so the sum runs over those objects, plus
    the two special cases
        o  -> it becomes a medoid, its distance drops from d(o,M) to 0,
        m  -> it loses its own cluster and takes min(d(m, M\\{m}), d(m, o)).
    For an attached object j:
        q(j) = d(j,o) - d(j,m)                                if d(j,o) <  d(j,m)
             = min(d(j,C2(j)), d(j,o)) - d(j,m)               otherwise
    with C2(j) the closest medoid other than m.
    """
    n, k = D.shape[0], len(medoids)
    md = D[:, medoids]
    nn = md.argmin(axis=1)                 # medoid each object is attached to
    d1 = md.min(axis=1)                    # and its distance
    medoid_set = set(medoids)
    costs = np.full((n, k), np.inf)
    for m_pos, m in enumerate(medoids):

        dm = md[:, m_pos]
        attached = nn == m_pos

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce claim C1 of "Ordinal time series analysis with the R package otsfeatures"
(arXiv:2304.12251, Section 4.3.2):

    PAM clustering (k = 4) on the 80 ordinal time series of otsfeatures::SyntheticData2,
    represented by the cumulative-probability features behind the distance dCC
    (`dataset_1` in the paper), scored with the Adjusted Rand Index against the four
    generating-process classes.

Everything is computed from the authors' own released artefacts:
  * the CRAN source tarball of `otsfeatures` (downloaded, cached, extracted) supplies
    `data/SyntheticData2.RData` and the reference R implementations of
    `c_marginal_probabilities` / `c_joint_probabilities`, which are ported line-by-line
    in src/otsfeatures_port.py;
  * src/pam.py is a deterministic port of the build+swap PAM that `cluster::pam` runs.

Usage
    python reproduce.py            # full target run (C1) + cheap companion claims
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # tiny 8-series / k=2 sanity run
    python reproduce.py --all      # also run the kNN / random forest / LDA claims (C5-C7)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist, squareform
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_rand_score

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "src"))

import download_otsfeatures as DL          # noqa: E402
import otsfeatures_port as OTS             # noqa: E402
from pam import pam                        # noqa: E402

STATES = (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)   # paper Sec. 4.1 / R11: states = 0:5 passed explicitly
LAGS = (1, 2)                 # paper Sec. 4.3.2 / R4: L = 2 (default option)
K = 4                         # paper Sec. 4.3.2 / R7: four generating processes
N_SERIES, T_LEN, N_CLASSES = 80, 600, 4


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(msg, flush=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- data checks
def check_dataset(series, classes, expect_groups=None):
    """Validate the collection against the paper's description (R1, R2, R12)."""
    n = len(series)
    lengths = {len(s) for s in series}
    vals = np.unique(np.concatenate([np.asarray(s) for s in series]))
    info = {
        "n_series": n,
        "series_lengths": sorted(int(l) for l in lengths),
        "distinct_values": [int(v) for v in vals],
        "class_counts": {int(c): int((classes == c).sum()) for c in np.unique(classes)},
    }
    assert all(v.is_integer() for v in vals), f"R2: values must be integers, got {vals}"
    assert set(vals.astype(int)) <= set(STATES), f"R2: values outside states {STATES}"
    assert len(vals) == len(STATES), f"R1/R2: expected all {len(STATES)} states to appear"
    assert len(classes) == n, "classes must align with data"
    assert not np.any(np.isnan(np.concatenate(series))), "no NA entries allowed"
    return info


def check_features(X, n_series):
    """Feature matrix sanity: shape, range, monotonicity of the cumulative blocks."""
    n_marg = len(STATES) - 1
    n_joint = (len(STATES) - 1) ** 2
    assert X.shape == (n_series, n_marg + len(LAGS) * n_joint), f"bad shape {X.shape}"
    assert np.isfinite(X).all(), "features must be finite"
    assert (X >= -1e-12).all() and (X <= 1 + 1e-12).all(), "cumulative probabilities in [0,1]"
    marg = X[:, :n_marg]
    assert np.all(np.diff(marg, axis=1) >= -1e-12), "marginal cdf nondecreasing in i"
    off = n_marg
    for _ in LAGS:
        block = X[:, off:off + n_joint].reshape(X.shape[0], len(STATES) - 1, len(STATES) - 1)
        assert np.all(np.diff(block, axis=1) >= -1e-12), "joint cdf nondecreasing in i"
        assert np.all(np.diff(block, axis=2) >= -1e-12), "joint cdf nondecreasing in j"
        off += n_joint
    return {"shape": list(X.shape),
            "blocks": {"marginal": n_marg, "joint_per_lag": n_joint, "lags": len(LAGS)}}


def manual_feature_check(series):
    """Recompute a few entries with explicit loops (independent of the vectorised port)."""
    s = np.asarray(series[0], dtype=np.float64)
    T = len(s)
    checks = []
    for i, st in enumerate(STATES[:-1]):
        cnt = 0
        for t in range(T):
            if s[t] <= st:
                cnt += 1
        checks.append((f"f_{st}", cnt / T, OTS.c_marginal_probabilities(s, STATES)[i]))
    for lag in LAGS:
        for i, si in enumerate(STATES[:-1]):
            for j, sj in enumerate(STATES[:2]):     # two columns are enough
                cnt = 0
                for t in range(lag, T):
                    if s[t] <= si and s[t - lag] <= sj:
                        cnt += 1
                checks.append((f"f_{si},{sj}(l={lag})", cnt / (T - lag),
                               OTS.c_joint_probabilities(s, STATES, lag=lag)[i, j]))
    worst = max(abs(a - b) for _, a, b in checks)
    assert worst < 1e-12, f"manual vs vectorised mismatch {worst}"
    return {"n_entries_checked": len(checks), "max_abs_diff": worst}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------ pipeline
def cluster_and_score(X, classes, k):
    d = pdist(X, metric="euclidean")          # R `dist()` default = Euclidean (R6)
    D = squareform(d)
    assert np.allclose(D, D.T) and np.allclose(np.diag(D), 0.0), "distance matrix invalid"
    assert (D[np.triu_indices_from(D, 1)] > 0).all(), "off-diagonal distances positive"
    res = pam(D, k)
    sizes = np.bincount(res["labels"], minlength=k)
    assert len(set(res["medoids"])) == k, "medoids must be distinct"
    assert sizes.min() > 0 and sizes.sum() == X.shape[0], "no empty clusters"
    # local optimality: no single swap may reduce the objective
    from pam import _swap_costs
    assert _swap_costs(D, res["medoids"])[np.isfinite(_swap_costs(D, res["medoids"]))].min() > -1e-9, \
        "PAM solution is not swap-optimal"
    ari = float(adjusted_rand_score(classes, res["labels"]))
    return res, ari, {"n_obs": int(X.shape[0]),

def objective(D: np.ndarray, medoids) -> float:
    """PAM total cost: sum over objects of the distance to their closest medoid."""
    return float(D[:, list(medoids)].min(axis=1).sum())


def _swap_costs(D: np.ndarray, medoids):
    """Exact cost change of every candidate swap (non-medoid o in, medoid m out).

    The classic Kaufman & Rousseeuw exchange shortcut only accounts for objects
    attached to m, so it can *under*-report an improving swap (objects attached to
    other medoids may also move closer to o) and stop early. With n = 80 and k = 4
    the full objective can simply be recomputed for all n*(k) candidates, which makes
    the descent exact; entry [o, m] is the true delta of that swap.
    """
    n, k = D.shape[0], len(medoids)
    medoid_set = set(medoids)
    base = objective(D, medoids)
    costs = np.full((n, k), np.inf)
    for m_pos, m in enumerate(medoids):
        rest = [x for p, x in enumerate(medoids) if p != m_pos]
        for o in range(n):
            if o in medoid_set:
                continue
            costs[o, m_pos] = objective(D, sorted(rest + [o])) - base
    del base
    return costs
